sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for bottom drawer
sections.what: Brings in the React library, the drawer component from the vaul library, and the class joining helper.
sections.why: The drawer needs the sliding panel component and styling tools.

sections.name: BottomDrawerProps
sections.title: Settings the drawer accepts
sections.what: Defines the props: the content, the element that opens the drawer, an optional title and description, and an optional extra class name.
sections.why: Lets any page use the same sliding panel with its own content.
sections.watch_out: The trigger must be a single element, because the drawer wraps it as a child.

sections.name: BottomDrawer
sections.title: Bottom sliding panel layout
sections.what: Draws a panel that rises from the bottom of the screen, covering most of the height, with a dim background behind it. It shows a small grip bar, an optional title and description, and the content.
sections.why: Gives a mobile style sheet for forms or detail views. Reason for the tall height is not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The panel height is fixed near full screen, so very short content may leave a large empty space. The content area has no scroll setting here, so long content may be cut off.

summary: A sheet that slides up from the bottom of the screen, aimed at phones, with an optional title, description and content.
purpose: Shows extra content such as forms or details without leaving the page.
why: Header says mobile-first app-like interaction. Likely reason: an app feel on phones.
how: A trigger element opens the drawer. The drawer shows a dark overlay, a small handle bar, an optional title and description, then the children. Tapping outside or dragging down closes it.
inputs: Children, the trigger element, an optional title, description and class name.
outputs: An opened or closed sheet. It does not change data.
risks: The height is set to almost the full screen, so bottom content may sit under the browser's controls on some phones. No close button is drawn in this file.
debug: If the drawer does not open, check the trigger element and that it responds to clicks. If it covers too much of the screen, check the class name passed in.
